A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility and utility of ctDNA testing for EGFR mutations in the clinical setting, and we have also identified a potential clinical trigger for ctDNA testing.
the use of liquid biopsy testing for T790M in NSCLC is feasible in clinical practice and can provide useful clinical information.
ctDNA T790M testing can effectively triage patients for treatment with EGFR T790 inhibitors, avoiding the need to perform invasive tissue biopsies in patients with advanced NSCLC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ddPCR test for T790M mutations is a reliable, non-invasive method for identifying patients with NSCLCs that have developed resistance to first-line EGFR TKI therapy.
ctDNA testing is a valuable and reliable tool for monitoring EGFR T790 resistance in NSCLC patients.
liquid biopsy testing is a useful and effective method for monitoring patients with NSCLClung cancer for the development of resistance to first-line therapy.
